title: unspoken dialogue
subject: book design
description: Unspoken Dialogue moves through the everyday ways that death, grief, and loss sit inside language, gesture, and memory, often without being named. Six conversations with people reflecting on these themes form a loose constellation of stories that circle around endings without resolving them. What emerges is less a single argument and more a durational encounter with how people speak, hesitate, redirect, and fall silent when asked to stay with death. By holding intimate narratives in a form that can be returned to, reread, and carried, the project opens a gentle, persistent space for reflection. In doing so, it suggests that design can accompany difficult conversations—not to solve or explain them, but to keep them possible, and keep them open.
summary: Unspoken Dialogue moves through the everyday ways that death, grief, and loss sit inside language, gesture, and memory, often without being named. Six conversations form a loose constellation of stories that circle around endings without resolving them.
details: research, interviewing, copywriting, InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop, bookbinding
risograph, laser, screen print, large-format printing (posters), UV-printed cover, spray-painted edges
tape bound, with a Swiss binding (the cover attached at the back, so the spine stays open)
deliverables: A [book](#book) holding all six conversations: the transcripts, a chart for each person, and closing thoughts on each, with an origami to fold.
A set of data-visualization [posters](#posters), the spoken and the unspoken, each drawn from one conversation.
Take-home [letter packets](#letter-packets), handed out at *Making Space 2026*.

sections.label: book
sections.text: All six conversations in one book. Each opens with a chart of how that person thinks about death, runs through the full transcript, and ends with closing thoughts and an origami to fold. Riso-printed skies, family photographs and fold-out pages sit between them.
sections.note: All six conversations: a chart for each person, the full transcript, and closing thoughts with an origami to fold.

sections.caption: Parts of the cover are printed in UV, so the chart only shows when the light catches it: a slight intangibility, like the line between what is spoken and what isn’t.

Printed on drafting paper, these pages fill the personal sections after each interview with photos, stories and text: the emotional, less tangible side of what was said. They layer over one another, so every turn makes a new layout.

media.caption: Each conversation’s closing section ends with an origami to fold, one for each person and chosen to echo their interview. Folding is meant to be meditative: less like making a wish, more like folding a thousand cranes for someone you care about.

sections.label: posters
sections.text: Two sets of three posters, each drawn from one conversation. The spoken set charts what was said; the unspoken set charts what wasn’t: silence, rhythm, and the emotions underneath.
sections.note: Two sets of three. The spoken set charts what was said; the unspoken set charts silence, rhythm and emotion.

media.caption: All six posters: spoken on top, unspoken below
Spoken: death, die and dying in 115 minutes of conversation
Unspoken: the rhythm of a conversation
Unspoken: changes in emotion within dialogue
Each poster with the origami from the same conversation.

sections.label: letter packets
sections.text: At *Making Space 2026*, visitors took home a letter packet: a letter, a reflection card, a graph for mapping their own relationship to death, a prompt card, and an origami to fold. It asked people to sit with their own experiences, not just read about others’.

title: contemplating death
subject: book design
description: This project is an exploration of mortality as a subject of contemplation rather than reaction. Often, we confront death through grief, loss, or tragedy: external events that force reflection. In this work, I sought to approach death on my own terms, to consider it holistically and without emotional catalysts. The resulting book is divided into six chapters that move from the most tangible forms of death to the most abstract, from grief and physical loss to dreams, spirituality, and the in-between. Structured through three recurring “voices”—white, gray, and black pages—the book invites readers into a cyclical process of questioning, absorbing, and reflecting. Each section prompts contemplation not only of death itself, but of how our understanding of mortality deepens our relationship with life.
summary:
Contemplating Death treats mortality as something to think through rather than react to. Death is usually met through grief, loss or tragedy, events that force reflection; this book approaches it slowly and on its own terms, with no emotional catalyst.

Built from found images and outside readings, gathered and sequenced into six chapters, it moves from the most tangible forms of death to the most abstract. It isn’t meant to be read once or rushed through: it offers no answers, only a space to pause, to question, and to return to as thoughts shift. Made as the first exploration for Unspoken Dialogue.
deliverables: A [book](#three-voices) in six chapters, from the most tangible forms of death to the most abstract.
A double-sided [index](#index) poster cataloguing every image in the book.
details: laser print, risograph (black pages), large-format printing (index poster)
sewn signatures, with a Swiss binding (the cover attached at the back, so the spine stays open)

sections.label: three voices
sections.text: Every chapter moves through three kinds of pages, each doing a different job:
items: White pages pose the question, opening each chapter with images.
Grey pages widen it, bringing in outside voices to inform.
Black pages turn inward, with a reflection.
sections.note: White pages pose the question. Grey pages bring in outside voices. Black pages turn inward.

sections.label: chapters
sections.text: Six chapters move from the most tangible forms of death to the most abstract. Along the way the cycle loosens, and colour slowly comes in.
sections.note: Six chapters, from the most tangible forms of death to the most abstract.

sections.caption: *Physical Death* is French-folded: its images are hidden inside the folds, faint enough that you can only half see them, holding both the shock of it and the distance.
Diagrams in the grey pages turn the readings into something visible, a first step towards the data-visualization posters of *Unspoken Dialogue*.

sections.label: index
sections.text: Every image in the book is catalogued on a double-sided poster: the images on one side, their page numbers, titles and makers on the other. The paper is thin enough that each side shows through.
sections.note: A double-sided poster cataloguing every image in the book; each side shows through the other.

title: lego sans
subject: typeface design
description: Lego Sans is a modular typeface that emerged from the process of printing with Lego letterpress. Built using only two Lego pieces, a square and a quarter-circle, the type took shape through hands-on assembly and experimentation.
summary: Lego Sans is a modular typeface that grew out of printing with Lego letterpress. Every letter is built from just two Lego pieces, a square and a quarter-circle, and the alphabet took shape through hands-on assembly and experimentation: set on a baseplate, inked, and pulled on a proof press.
deliverables: A modular typeface built from two Lego pieces, for now in print only.
An alphabet book, one letter per page, printed by Lego letterpress.

media.caption: Each letter is built by hand on a Lego baseplate from squares and quarter-circles, mirrored so it prints the right way round.

title: kowloon
subject: book design
description: Kowloon is a dual-layered  book that contrasts the historical reality of the Kowloon Walled City with its fictionalized portrayals in popular media. Once a self-regulated enclave shaped by geopolitical tensions, the city has become a cyberpunk icon, often depicted as a chaotic, futuristic labyrinth.Designed as two books within one, the piece features perforated pages that readers can tear open, revealing the hidden "fiction" layer beneath the "reality" section.  The "reality" section takes an academic, text-based approach, while the "fiction" layer is more image-driven, reflecting how history transforms into myth.
summary: A book that contrasts the historical reality of the Kowloon Walled City with its fictional portrayals in popular media. Once a self-regulated enclave shaped by geopolitical tensions, the city has become a cyberpunk icon, often shown as a chaotic, futuristic labyrinth.
deliverables: Two books in one. Perforated pages tear open to reveal a hidden “fiction” layer beneath the “reality” section: the reality layer is academic and text-based, the fiction layer image-driven, showing how history turns into myth.

title: 76 cones
subject: book design
description: 76 Cones explores my psychogeographic journey documenting 76 traffic cones in New York City. The book unfolds in four parts: a layered flyer that introduces the cone as an object, a translucent paper booklet mapping my movement between each cone, an index cataloging my reflections at each site, and a fold-out sheet showing how, over time, the cones lost their objectivity and became simply the color orange. Bound in an orange file folder with office supply-inspired binding, the book evokes construction and urban spaces' bureaucratic and municipal nature.
summary: A psychogeographic journey documenting 76 traffic cones across New York City, and how, over time, they stopped being objects and became simply the color orange.
deliverables: A book in four parts, bound in an orange file folder with office-supply-inspired binding: a layered flyer introducing the cone as an object, a translucent booklet mapping the route between each cone, an index of reflections from each site, and a fold-out sheet of the cones turning into pure orange.

title: the joy luck supper club
subject: print design
description: The Joy Luck Supper Club is a social campaign supporting small businesses in NYC’s Chinatown. Inspired by the title of the famous book, *The Joy Luck Club*, the campaign celebrates the vibrant culture and family-run establishments of Chinatown. It features an event flyer and an interactive map. The flyer is printed using Risograph and styled after Chinese takeout menus, while the website map highlights local vendors, serving as a guide to the neighbourhood’s businesses.

title: what is a keeb
subject: web design
description: What is a Keeb? is a fun and interactive digital collection of custom mechanical keyboards. The website features a sorting feature to help users explore builds by color, materials, and mods. To add an extra layer of engagement, the introductory blurb is coded as a typing test, making it a playful resource for both newcomers and enthusiasts passionate about the world of mechanical keyboards.

title: conversations
subject: zine design
description: Conversations is zine that reflects on evolving familial bonds through text messages between me and my parents after moving away for college. It’s printed on translucent vellum paper overlaying old photos of my parents and I. With the addition of ephemeral inserts relating to the conversations in our texts, the book aims to evoke a sense of nostalgia and the idea of memories as fleeting. Each page offers a glimpse into the past, highlighting the impermanence of both life and printed form.

title: wang kar wai
subject: book design
description: Wang Kar Wai is a tribute to the renowned filmmaker, celebrating his signature use of color and framing. The book features full-bleed pages and layered frame-within-a-frame layouts, with fold-out spreads that capture the fluid motion present in his films. His name is laser-cut in the cover with iconic stills from his films peeking through to represent his clever use of framing within his work. Small touches, like binding with red thread and spreads that recreate the typographic panels seen in his films, further alluded to his artistic style.
summary: A tribute to the filmmaker, celebrating his signature use of color and framing.
deliverables: A book with full-bleed pages, layered frame-within-a-frame layouts, and fold-out spreads that capture the motion of his films. His name is laser-cut into the cover so stills peek through, the binding is sewn with red thread, and some spreads recreate the typographic panels from his films.

title: roshomon
subject: web design
description: Roshomon is an immersive web experience that brings Ryūnosuke Akutagawa's short story Roshomon to a new format. Set against the backdrop of societal breakdown and calamity in Kyoto, the website delves into themes of morality, desperation, and the complexity of human nature. Through interactive storytelling and sensory elements, users are invited to navigate the moral dilemmas faced by the protagonist, mirroring the harsh realities of survival in a world engulfed by chaos. Designed only with typography the website challenges conventional storytelling norms and offers users a reflective exploration of the human condition.

title: the commute
subject: web design
description: The commute is a web design that translate a concrete poem about the beauty in the mundane into the digital space. Inspired by the my daily commute, the website uses typography and layout to create a rhythmic visual narrative. Through subtle animations and interactive elements you can experience the ebb and flow of city life and the moments of reflection and revelation amidst the chaos of the commute.

title: astrological calendar
subject: book design
description: Astrological Calendar is a daily calendar that is modelled after my friend’s birth chart. Each day communicates her horoscope, the moon phase, the position of the earth and the moon relative to the sun, and the current astrological sign. It comes in a set of 2 and is spiral bound.

title: iconic ghibli food
subject: web design
description: Iconic Ghibli Food showcases to some the delicious food featured in Studio Ghibli films. From the comforting bowls of ramen in ponyo to the hearty breakfast in Howl's Moving Castle, this simple website showcases the most iconic food moments from the Ghibli movie.

title: code-switching
subject: book design
description: Code-switching is a risograph-printed book that visually embodies the concept of code-switching. Using an accent color and distinct language for each chapter, the design reflects the overlapping nature of language shifts. Using the contents from the code-switching wikipedia page, real-life conversations illustrating code-switching were added for authenticity. The Risograph medium introduces a tactile element, emphasizing the dynamic quality of navigating multiple languages. This book serves as a tangible exploration of the nuanced art of code-switching, inviting readers to appreciate the intricacies of linguistic diversity in our daily interactions.
